title: Inner-layer Token Self-modulation as Another Scaling Axis for LLMs
claim: A lightweight token-indexed lookup branch modulates the backbone's FFN update, and a routed mixture of such modulators generalizes it at negligible compute.
layout: 3 panels, bottom-to-top data flow, side modules feeding a central Transformer block
description: Architecture diagram with three rounded gray panels. The center panel shows a Transformer layer drawn bottom-to-top: RMSNorm, Attention, residual add, RMSNorm, MLP, a multiply node, and a final add node, with residual loops at the sides. The left panel is the simple variant. A token id x indexes a gray embedding table (entries 1…V, with row x highlighted green), then Norm & Scale and +1, and the result feeds the multiply node after the MLP. The right panel is the mixture variant. A Router takes the hidden state and selects among a pool of table rows (x:1 … x:n, with a few highlighted green). Their outputs are multiplied by the router weights, summed, passed through Norm & Scale, and added back into the residual stream. Peach boxes, green highlights, and orange dashed arrows mark the lookup and routing paths. The eye goes first to the central block, then to the arrows linking the two side modules.
caption: Architecture of JTok/JTok-M. JTok (left) augments each Transformer layer with a tokenindexed table. Each token retrieves a modulation vector, applies norm and a learnable per-dimension scaling, and forms a lightweight multiplicative gate to modulate the FFN update via element-wise products. JTok-M (right) generalizes JTok by maintaining a pool of token-indexed modulators and using a router conditioned on the hidden state to select a sparse Top-K mixture per token; the mixed modulator is normalized+scaled and injected as an additional residual alongside the backbone update. Both are plug-in bypass modules implemented with table lookups and element-wise operations, allowing retrieval to be overlapped with backbone and adding negligible compute.
abstract: LLMs have traditionally scaled along dense dimensions, where performance is coupled with near-linear increases in computational cost. While MoE decouples capacity from compute, it introduces large memory overhead and hardware efficiency challenges. To overcome these, we propose token-indexed parameters as a novel, orthogonal scaling axis that decouple model capacity from FLOPs. Specifically, we introduce ReToken and MoRT, which augment Transformer layers with modulation vectors retrieved from auxiliary embedding tables. These vectors modulate the backbone via lightweight, element-wise operations, incurring negligible FLOPs overhead. Extensive experiments on both dense and MoE backbones, spanning from 190M to 9.8B parameters, demonstrate that our approach consistently reduces validation loss and significantly improves downstream task performance (e.g., +7.3 on ARC-C, +6.3 on GSM8K). Rigorous isoFLOPs analysis further confirms that MoRT fundamentally shifts the quality–compute Pareto frontier, achieving comparable model quality with 35\% less compute relative to vanilla MoE architectures, and we validate that token-indexed parameters exhibit a predictable power-law scaling behavior. Moreover, our efficient implementation ensures that the overhead introduced by ReToken and MoRT remains marginal.
